# gift_registry_services — rework round 2 claims

- T0-1 → tasks/0.json evaluation_criteria[3].objective no longer claims a rewards reversal entry (it states that the registry has none); evaluation_criteria[7].necessity no longer claims a circle rewards bonus (it states that the missed accrual reads no Finch Circle input, and that the Platinum tier feeds only the completion Finch Circle bonus). The neighbouring read-step texts (find_registries, find_purchases, find_card_accounts) were re-swept against the revised charter. The scored values of task 0 are unchanged.
- T1-1 / G-10 → registry_ext_credit_redemption: the old payable factor is relabelled `parameter` (credit_payable_amount). The method is now credit_bonus_form, whose tiers change the shape of the credit drawn: division by one plus the bonus percent for an item still wanted, a reduction capped at a bonus base for a fully given item, and the identity (no bonus) for an item not on the registry. The former item stretch factor is folded into this method, and the ladder conditions are not repeated elsewhere. Task 1's gold, computations, factor_trace, factor_sensitivity, baseline_result, argument tracing, prerequisite_closure, solvability business effects and design_rationale are recomputed and re-stated.
- G-1 → unchanged (watch). On task 0's world the only guest gift entry without an accrual is the most recent one, so the resolver closes the edge. The accrual rule now also states that a gift already carrying a reversal is not accrued.
- G-2 → unchanged (watch). On task 1's world exactly one received return lacks a credit, and it is the latest received return.
- G-3 → closed: registry_ext_missed_rewards_accrual's rule now states that a guest gift entry whose gift already carries a rewards reversal entry is not accrued by the policy.
- G-4 → unchanged (observation). On both worlds the membership's latest tier change precedes the dated occurrence, so the current tier equals the dated tier. Task 0 tracing now cites the tier-change date.
- G-5 → closed: the completion redemption's no-discount tier (compute and rule) now also covers lines of the Fine Jewelry & Watches and Designer Handbags & Luxury classes, through a new line-class read.
- G-6 → closed: the cardholder rewards bonus now tests elite and other active card accounts by account existence. The ladder states that the second tier applies only when no elite account is held, so a second active account cannot change the tier.
- G-7 → closed: the return credit no longer reads the furniture-only restocking waiver tier parameter. The restocking ladder rests on condition, reason and days since the event.
- G-8 → closed: the post-event item value is now a share of the type's completion discount percent, and the standard-card tier is the greater of the type card bonus and a standard card bonus. No tier repeats its fall-through on any registry type.
- G-9 → closed: the deduction-ceiling method is replaced by restock_taper_shape. Its tiers are no restocking charge for duplicates, a marginal schedule (full percent up to a threshold, half percent above) for large gifts, and a proportional charge otherwise.
- G-11 → unchanged (observation on blueprint claim.event_types, which is outside the write domain). The accrual and credit-use events remain registry-category writes of this difficulty alone.
- Realism (late charge on returns inside the published window) → removed. In its place are an open-box grace (opened gifts returned soon after the occasion pay a reduced restocking percent) and an insured return surcharge for valuable gifts sent back by label or pickup.
- Realism (credit "stretch") → reframed as a registry credit bonus with a published form. The period ladder's fall-through (a line bought before the event) is reachable by customers of the write.
- Whole class (every method factor changes the formula's shape) → the four method factors are markdown_better_of (none / better-of with a floor / plain percent), large_gift_taper (marginal / none / proportional), restock_taper_shape (none / marginal / proportional) and credit_bonus_form (division / capped reduction / identity).
- Whole class (ladders, rounding, overwrites) → every ladder now states its precedence explicitly ("any other", "where no elite account is held", "otherwise (…)"). Every rounding sentence says half up to the cent, once, on the final amount, matching the single RND on the result. Every overwrite keeps a replaced_by that names its own scope and the scope left under base. compute_basis quotes were re-checked as verbatim sentences of each rule.
- Observations in 1.md → why_false now cites the returned purchase's returned_date field instead of an unrecorded receipt date. Each multi-source label in task 1's rationale now matches a tier test that combines distinct records. The seed-consistency texts for the towel credit and the glasses credit use are restated under the revised rules.
